_about: Source of CHANGE_LIST.md and proposed/en_with_proposals.md. PROPOSALS ONLY: none is applied to the product, none is legal advice, none is approved. Each proposal states a change to the English text so that the text matches what the code does (or states a fact the text is silent about). Wording that makes a legal commitment is flagged for counsel and left in square brackets where an owner or counsel must supply the content. Every approved proposal would need translation into all seven offered languages and a native legal review (LG-10) before it ships.

proposals.proposed: Basic is free. Premium is a preview plan that is not available for purchase yet. Nothing is charged, and this page will be updated before any payment is offered.
proposals.reason: The current sentence says Premium is EUR 19.99 per month and is selected online after account creation. Today there is no purchase path, live billing is disabled by a code constant and external checkout is not authorised.

proposals.proposed: To use your data rights, open Data & Privacy in your account: you can download your data, delete your account, or submit a privacy request for a person to follow up. [Owner and counsel to supply: the name of the organisation responsible for this service and a privacy contact address.]
proposals.reason: The current text points to a support address configured for the deployment. No such address exists in the configuration, so the sentence has nothing to point to. The in-app paths do exist.

proposals.proposed: files you upload (for example a CV) stored privately under a random key, never a public URL, and the claims detected in them (short verbatim snippets you review). The full text of a document is read from the stored file when needed and is not stored separately.
proposals.reason: The text says OCR-extracted text and detected claims are stored. The code stores the claims; the whole extracted text is not stored.

proposals.proposed: AI features send the text needed to produce a response to a model provider (currently through OpenRouter): your messages, Memory summaries you approved, the text of a job description you select, evidence snippets from your documents that you approved, your Practice answers and stories you select. Your original files are never sent. Secrets are never sent.
proposals.reason: The current sentence says only that necessary text is sent. The categories are broader than that suggests (DF-01). Naming a provider is a recipient-disclosure decision for counsel.

proposals.proposed: Where semantic search is configured, the text of your search question is sent to an embedding provider to find matching sources.
proposals.reason: A second processor receives query text when a semantic embedding provider is configured; the text does not mention it.

proposals.proposed: Current-market research (optional) may query an external job-market service and may read the public website of a company you name.
proposals.reason: The code fetches a company website only when the candidate supplies it; the text says only job-market sources.

proposals.proposed: request identifiers, timestamps, coarse event categories and audit records of privileged or security-relevant actions. Audit records hold metadata only (identifiers, states and counts), never your documents, answers or messages.
proposals.reason: 05E restricts audit context to an allow-list of metadata keys at one choke point; the text can now state it. Counsel to decide whether the identifiers themselves are personal data.

proposals.proposed: You can export your data and permanently delete your account and its application-controlled data (documents, private files, Practice history, Memory, Story Bank and sessions). If a private file cannot be removed, nothing is removed and you can try again. Preparation chats created before ownership records existed and never reopened may not be found for deletion.
proposals.reason: States the files-first deletion behaviour and the stated limit of the chat ownership index, both true in the code after 05E.

proposals.proposed: Ask4Mo keeps your content until you delete it. [Owner and counsel to supply: any fixed retention period for content, authentication records and audit records.]
proposals.reason: No fixed retention period exists today (PRIV-RET). The text is silent; a retention statement is a policy and legal decision.

proposals.proposed: When you acknowledge the Terms, the Privacy notice or the AI transparency page in Settings, Ask4Mo records which version, when, and from where in the product (no IP address or device). Accounts created before this existed have no record.
proposals.reason: Acceptance recording exists (W10.10) and 05E adds the user's own history. Only the Settings source is wired; registration records nothing.

proposals.proposed: Staff access: administrators see account and usage metadata. They cannot open your documents, answers, conversations, Memory or evidence through the product.
proposals.reason: True of the application permissions. Direct database or hosting-console access is outside the application and is a hosting matter; counsel decides how it is described.

proposals.proposed: Registration is by invitation during the private beta.
proposals.reason: Registration requires an invitation in every hosted environment; the Terms do not say so.

proposals.proposed: Mo may consult bounded specialists (role and opportunity, evidence, coaching) through an allow-list of tools.
proposals.reason: The current sentence adds 'with server-side revalidation'. Revalidating every model-requested tool call is package 01D, not merged at the commit this pack was written against. Restore the phrase only after 01D is merged and re-verified.
